591:### F2 Summon on the fly
592-- Asked:       "A captain will move to the station position, emit the call when reaching the station arrival point,
593-               but then keep moving without stopping. In the basic case of a captain setting up on a single PR, it
594-               saves the stop and go nature of it (while still correlating the objects because the captain's call
595-               blip should match the arrival effect of the station)."
596-- Today:       Station jump-in (`facility.enter`, 2.8 s: tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600; E1 retired the
597-               beacon pulses) flies the summoner to a spot beside the station, holds it there through the arrival
598-               and a second named (`crewHoldMs`, 22 B9), then flies it back over 0.8 s (`stationJumpIn.ts`).
599-               Summons aren't director moments (not protected), so no lever shortens them, and they aren't in
600-               the crowd's `ARRIVING` set.
601-- Decided:     The summoner's path passes through the spot without stopping. As it passes, it gives **one call
602-               blip**, and the station jumps in at that instant, in the same hue and with the same ring shape, so the
603-               two read as one cause and effect (R8, R10). The hold and the fly-back go. The ship carries on to
604-               its next place: its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), else its rest beside its work (13 §4).
605-               The summoner is named from the blip (E2: plates from the act) and its plate rides with the ship
606-               for `NOTE_MIN_MS`. The rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival (a 15 §7 row). Under
607-               reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place.
608-- Acceptance:
609-  - A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors.
610-  - A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place, and the station's act
611-    starts within 50 ms of the blip.
612-  - 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated, and the packet names each change.
613-  - The ledger shows the saving per pod.
614-- Risk:        schedule (medium: every pod with a summon).
615-- Touches:     `theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts`, `engine/pace.ts` (`facility.enter` phases),
616-               `chart/fx/commands.ts` (`pursue` passing through), 13 §6, 05 §8 (M-row of the jump-in), 15 §7.
617-- Depends on:  F1
618-- State:       open
619-
620-### F3 Summon chains
621-- Asked:       "In the chained case ... he would basically move smoothly around the star system as stations appear in
622-               succession behind him (likely only fractions of a second between their activation) without [the]
623-               ship stopping ... Any action that summons a station within a short time period by the same captain
624-               (EG, same or adjacent workday OR within 30 seconds of the playback time) should just execute a
625-               smooth, chained maneuver like this."
626-- Today:       Each summon is its own `facility.enter`, and each station's first PR opening (`attachment.open`)
627-               waits for it. The nearest pattern is E7's Sector sweep (M-32): one carrier draft in place of many
628-               (`sweepCreations`, `PlannedManeuver.sweep`), revealing each piece in turn, with one note; and
629-               B-21/B-22's fuse, which joins raw beats into one without re-timing an event.
630-- Decided:     A **summon chain**: `facility.enter` drafts with one summoner, each link within `CHAIN_WINDOW_MS`
631-               (30 s, 15 §10) in x of the link before (a chain, so the window slides, unlike the volley's from its
632-               first), **or** on the same or the next working day (weekends skipped, the viewer's zone, as B-12).
633-               Two links or more. The links' raw beats fuse (B-21, amended: a chain's fuse may cross **one** day
634-               turn, F-Q1), under the same B-15 guard as `volleysOf`; a link the guard refuses starts a new chain, and nothing else
635-               breaks it (F-Q6). No event is re-timed (B-14) and a seek snaps to the fused beat's end state (INV-15); across a day turn, the day rule is F4's (Days). The first link
636-               carries one new rule, *Summons run* (`facility.run`, phases scaled by the count, like
637-               `sweepPhases`), in place of the links' own drafts. The ship flies one smooth path through each
638-               link's spot (F2), each station jumping in as it passes, `CHAIN_STEP_MS` apart at most (about
639-               300 ms, 15 §10); each station's tender launches with its station.
640-               **Visit order is proximity, not time** (decided 2026-11-06): every chain's path (F3's and F4's)
641-               runs one way round the system, all clockwise or all counter-clockwise, taking the next station
642-               along in that direction, never the next by its PR's time, so the ships move in an arc or spiral
643-               instead of dashing back and forth. The direction is the one that gives the shorter sweep from the
644-               captain's start, from the plan's places (pure in world terms, so seek and play agree; a new pure
645-               `chainOrder.ts` beside `sweepOrder.ts`). The stations are different pieces, so B-15 doesn't fix
646-               their order.
647-               Labels: the summoner is named; the stations come in at rest (T4) and claim no attention slots; one
648-               note names the count in the source's words (R9, R12; the wording is the planner's, e.g. *PRs into
649-               36 Repositories*). History keeps every event's row, and its *now* mark walks the visit order.
650-- Acceptance:
651-  - Unit tests: grouping is deterministic over the goldens; both window conditions chain, and F1's bounding cases

## How the user likes to work
- **Brainstorm, then a few focused questions, then build.** They answer questions inline in the plan
  file, or through multiple-choice prompts. Offer a recommendation, not a survey.
- **They review in `npm run dev`, the gallery, and from stills.** End each pass with stills (a drive
  run's `test-results/drive/<steps>/`, or a spec's `test-results/*.png`) and the exact scene and
  moment to watch.
- **They often send notes mid-task.** Fold them into the current work and say how you read them.
- **Build mode, per block** (2026-10-14): propose inline work (with one fresh-context reviewer) or a
  workflow, with a rough time and cost, and let them choose. A workflow runs only if they ask for one.
  Since v1.4, work runs through the Sluice; the user sets each block's run size (full or lean) in 27's Decisions.
- **Questions one at a time** (2026-11-06): when closing out open questions, ask them one by one, each with a
  recommendation, and record each answer in the scope doc's Open questions and Decisions.
- **Check the branch first** (2026-11-06): live work may be on a `flow/<tranche>` branch (or with another
  dev), not `main`. Read `git log main..HEAD` and the scope doc's States before planning.
- **They start the Sluice in a fresh chat** to save context; leave the scope doc and this note ready for it.
- They commit planning and doc changes themselves; under the Sluice, the orchestrator commits each accepted item. Never `volta install` (Node 24 is pinned per
  project).
- Toy prototype rules: public npm is fine, momentum matters, and the docs in `docs/` are the source of
  truth (update 02/03 in the same change when departing from them).

## Direction we converged on (keep it)
Checked against the code on 2026-10-13. Where v1 changed a direction, the item says so; the values
are in [15](../15-reference.md).
- **Pace: "a cozy campfire, not fireworks."** At 1× an episode fits a 45 s budget (`BUDGET_MS`; it
  was about 60 s until slice 6); 4× is the lively quick look. Every beat finishes its choreography
  before the next one starts. (In Solar, merges and essential beats may run past the budget; that row was closed on 2026-10-27,
  episode length accepted: 23 §5.)
- **Story grammar:** tell → act → land → echo, along geometry that already exists (orbits, routes,
  spokes). Solar's maneuvers add `gather` and `disperse` around it ([15 §7](../15-reference.md#7-maneuvers)).
  A finished round ends on its finale, not just the recap bloom (13 §6.4).
- **Continuity:** nothing teleports. The glide layer eases every node, pursuit chases live goals,
  lines draw on rather than popping in, and a seek snaps (INV-15).
- **Motion has to earn its place:** essential, narrative, and ornament tiers, gated by a volatility
  meter (at Maximum, the default, the load marks don't apply). A move worth "only an inch" just
  glides (v0 views).
- **Ships help; they never attack.** A broad, soft **tractor beam** replaced every thin "laser" beam;
  it was cyan, and is given blue now (`TRACTOR`, 15 §2). (v1 amends this: in the Solar view ships
  and stations also fight threats, and only threats, in hero blue; only threats fire red; 02 INV-08.)
  - A ship rests where its captain last worked (by recorded `changedBy`/authorship, not by
    assignment) and stays there. No commuting back to the parent. (Solar: a resting captain idles
    beside the work, 13 §4.)
  - Long streaks across the screen are for navigation only (jump trails).
- **The review formation:** at a PR merge, the author leads at the point with the tractor beam, and
  the approvers fly the wings and stream gold **support** into the author. No role chips: the beams
  tell who led and who supported, and guests wear their captain's picture like any ship while
  playing. It celebrates the team and never ranks anyone (INV-19). (v0 views. Solar's Power link
  keeps the idea: approvers' given-blue energy chains to the author, then the station; 13 §6.)
- **Task radar (v0 views):** Tasks sit in bands by rung (Ready on the outside, Accomplished hugging the planet),
  each on a fixed spoke. The Story's label carries a tally. Hover-only labels for Tasks that aren't
  Underway.
- **Dynamic labels:** compact (title only) while playing or moving; ships show only their captain's
  picture, hugging the top of the ship; full labels return about 3 s after things settle; a new or
  moved Task flashes its title (v0). Solar adds the expanded tier: a pointed or selected object's
  mega-label, and holo plates on planets, stations and ships ([15 §6](../15-reference.md#6-labels-and-type)).
- **Art:** mechanical objects (ships, stations, vessels) take no paint filter; celestial bodies do.
  People's names are ivory. Gold means accomplished (09 signal ladder).

# 27 — v1.4: scope

**Status:** scoped 2026-10-29 with the user (`/sluice scope`), from the intake opened the same day when v1.3 closed.
Earlier plan: [archive/23-v1.3.md](archive/23-v1.3.md). Workflow: the sluice (`designDoc` in
`.claude/sluice/config.json`). Work files: `docs/progress/v1.4/`. v1.4 is the first tranche run under the sluice, so
its records stay apart from v1.3's. Fixture data only (INV-18).

## Goal

v1.4 finishes v1.3's leftovers and makes playback **a story more than a history**. Pulsar Pod (20 captains)
plays within a target time set from measured numbers, while Comet Pod (solo) keeps its full drama. Busy work
is told in fewer, larger moments that still name every cause (R13) and make every participant a hero.
Formations form up on screen and clear of their beams, with labels that don't collide. The chart rests
quieter: only what you point at, what you select and what playback emphasizes gets a full plate. v1.4 is
done when every item below is accepted, the human gates are signed, the frame budget (p95 ≤ 2 vsyncs) holds
on Pulsar under the profiles that bake the aura (`phone`, `tablet`; C3), with `desktop` and `laptop-battery`
reported soft with numbers at the final check (amended 2026-11-06), and 90-later holds only what was deferred
here.

## Rules

- The standing rules R1–R14: [13 §1](13-game-design.md#design-pillars). Most cited here: R1 (holo labels, four
  tiers), R8 (every motion means something), R9 (the drawn count is the true count), R10 (identity by more
  than one cue), R11 (an object arrives before its label), R12 (the ADO word first), R13 (playback explains
  itself), R14 (attention is budgeted).
- The invariants: [02 §1](02-domain-rules.md#1-invariants), especially INV-12 and INV-15 (playing to *x* and
  seeking to *x* draw the same thing), INV-14 (stable slots), INV-18 (fixture data only) and INV-19 (no
  individual scoring).
- Story time's B-15 (05 §8.3a): order within a piece is never broken.
- Values go to [15](15-reference.md) in the same change. Departures from 02 and 03 are amended there and
  called out.
- Project lenses for the sluice's agents: `.claude/sluice/project.md`.

## Order and blocks

| Block | Items | Why this order | Human gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A1, A2, A3, A4 | Quick carried fixes. A3's vsync budget is the yardstick B1 is measured against | Final check |
| B | B1, B2, B3, B4 | The carried looks. B1 (resting plates) goes first: it changes every scene's labels, which D and E lay out against | Final check |

## Acceptance

- The pod opens in `npm run dev` with 36 stations on its rings, with no layout overlap (VC-3 case).
- The ledger has the pod's row, measured before F2.

How to read it (decided here): **"its halcyon golden"** means two things. The Meteor scope's new entry in `sprint-pods.scenes.json`, which appears by itself. And a new Solar golden for this pod only, `halcyon-meteor.{plan,scenes}.json`, so F2 to F4 have a diff to read. **"36 stations"** are the run's 36. The pod has 37: the run's 36 plus the lone summon's station, which a single-summon case needs (a summon always brings a new station). The e2e checks that all 36 run repos are drawn and that the total is 37.

## Approach
1. **The pod is Meteor Pod** (`Halcyon Reach\Meteor Pod`, area 8005, a favorite). The name fits a shower of 36 in a minute. Comet is hand-written, and this pod is too: a `meteor(): PodBuild` in `pods.ts`, with a loop for the 36. Item ids are 12001+ (today's highest is 11227), PR ids 21001+ (today's highest is 20764), and the new Feature is **9018 'Platform upkeep'**. Meteor goes last everywhere (areas, repos, people, events, runs), so nothing that exists moves.
2. **Cast.** `cast.ts` is generated, so extend `scripts/find-cast.ts` and re-run it (`npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts scripts/find-cast.ts`). After `const comet = …`, add `const meteor = pick(8, { hulls: true, colours: true }, <fresh have sets>)`. After `cometRepo`, add `const meteorRepos = pickRepos(37, new Set(), new Set())`. Emit `METEOR_CAST` after `PULSAR_CAST` (offset 49), and `METEOR_REPOS` after `PULSAR_REPOS`. The picks are greedy over a shared `used` set, so appending them leaves every existing line byte-identical. **Check that `git diff` on cast.ts only adds lines.** The roles go by index: [0] **A**, the run's captain; [1] **B**, the other captain; [2] **C**, the second author; [3..7] **D–H**, approvers who hold no items (like Quasar's manager). `METEOR_REPOS[0..35]` are the run's repos and `[36]` is the lone summon's.
3. **The timeline, exactly as given.** Times are UTC and the zone is America/Los_Angeles, so every time below falls on the same local date. Every item is made at planning (Fri 11 Sep, 18:00–18:20Z) in S41/Meteor. Stories and the Bug have parent 9018, and Tasks have their Story as parent. With no creations inside the round, there is no opening sweep. When a PR opens while its item is Active, add `column(item, 'Code Review')`, as `emitItem` does. Every PR gets `prStats` from `prStatsFor(<PrPlan-shaped object>, METEOR handles)`.
   - **A's run, S1 12001 'Move every service to the new base image'.** Tasks: 12002 'Write the upgrade script' and 12003 'Open the PRs'. S1 goes Ready Mon 14 17:00 and Active Tue 15 16:30. Task 12002 goes Active at 16:35 and Closed at 21:00. Task 12003 goes Active at 21:30 and Closed Wed 16 16:50.

## Acceptance

How to read it (decided here): **"its halcyon golden"** means two things. The Meteor scope's new entry in `sprint-pods.scenes.json`, which appears by itself. # Tests, and how to iterate quickly

**Status:** current as of 2026-10-27 (through v1.3 Block B). The e2e specs and goldens are named below, and the unit tests and
drive steps mostly are; the v1.2 tests and steps are listed in the v1 table's v1.2 rows.

Decided 2026-10-07: the full e2e suite takes minutes, so iteration runs a few of its pieces, and the
full suite runs once before handing back.

| Command | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | Unit and golden (Vitest) | ~5 s |
| `npm run e2e:keystone` | One path per area, tagged `@keystone`, specs in parallel | ~40 s |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- <name…>` | Named specs, e.g. `npm run e2e:spec -- explore slice4` | per spec |
| `npm run e2e` | Everything: the specs in parallel, then the pixel and frame-time specs alone | ~3 min |
| `npm run bake:asteroids` | Re-bake `assets/atlas/asteroids.{png,json}` from the procedural asteroids through the gallery (23 C7); `asteroid-atlas.spec.ts` checks the atlas path renders (no missing frames) with its flag on | seconds |
| `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` | Launch the app, run steps, keep screenshots, state, console, and dev log | seconds |

**While iterating:** run the specs for what changed (below), plus `e2e:keystone` once things look
right. Run `npm run e2e` once before handing work back.

## Windows don't appear (decided 2026-10-09)

`npm run e2e` never shows its windows: they were opening centred, over whatever you were doing. A
hidden window still animates (`backgroundThrottling` is off in test mode) and Playwright still
composites it, so the pixel baselines and the review stills are unaffected — the whole suite passes
hidden.

- **To watch a run:** `STAR_CHART_TEST_SHOW=1 npm run e2e` (or any single spec). The window is pinned
  to the top-left of the primary display, and opens without taking focus.
- **`STAR_CHART_TEST_DPR=2`** launches with that devicePixelRatio (default 1), for checks that depend on it.
- **`npm run drive`** always shows its window: watching the app is the point of it.

## Taking ADO away (slice 5)

The fake ADO org can be switched off mid-run, from the main process, with no test-only surface in
production: `app.evaluate(() => globalThis.__starChartFakeTransport.offline = true)` (see
`tests/e2e/offline.spec.ts`). Three more affordances, all test-mode only:
- `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL` (a regex on the URL) with `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL_STATUS` (500 by default; 401
  for a dead token, 403/404 for a refusal that keeps the last known facts).
- `STAR_CHART_PROJECTS_TTL_MS=1`: the project list is normally remembered for 30 s, which would hide an
  offline start; this asks every time, as a real launch does.
- The `reboot()` and `forgetScopes()` test hooks start the app's data over, as a launch does.

## Which specs cover what

## Shared helpers (`tests/e2e/launch.ts`)

`launchApp`, `settle`, `clickNode`, `enterNodeByKey`, `keyOf`, the v0 walks (`openCometCrew`,
`openFeature101`) and `launchGallery` live here, and so does **`frames(page, n = 2)`** (23 F5): it
resolves once the page has drawn `n` more frames. Read what a seek or a setter drew after
`await frames(page)`, never after a fixed `waitForTimeout`, which under load can pass with no frame
drawn; don't write another copy in a spec. (In-page loops that sample every frame,
`await new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(r))` inside one `page.evaluate`, are samplers, not
waits, and stay where they are.)

**Waiting under load.** A machine running four specs draws fewer, longer frames, and the chart's
clock advances at most 100 ms a frame (`ChartApp.ts`). So bound a played stretch by the playhead
(`session().x`) or by the condition itself (the body arrived, enough moves judged), not by wall time:
`board`'s travel runs until the body arrives (bounded by 8 s of playhead), and `solar-dense`'s facing
check plays until 30 decisive moves are judged. To prove a de-flake, run the spec under load, e.g.
`npx playwright test --grep @keystone &` beside `npx playwright test <spec> --repeat-each=3` (build once
first, `npx electron-vite build`: the two runs share `out/`).

**Touch.** `touch.spec.ts` sends real touches through the DevTools protocol
(`page.context().newCDPSession(page)`, `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`): Playwright's `touchscreen` needs a
context made with `hasTouch`, which an Electron window can't be given. Chromium turns them into touch
events and pointer events with `pointerType: 'touch'`, as a touchscreen would.

## Isolation and parallel runs

Every launch gets its own `userData` (`tests/e2e/launch.ts`): never the developer's real cache. A spec
that relaunches on the same cache passes `STAR_CHART_DB_DIR`, and its `userData` sits beside that
folder. Specs run four at a time (`E2E_WORKERS` to change it). Tests inside a spec run in order; most
share one app and walk a story, so a test can depend on the ones before it. Keystone tests are chosen
to pass on their own after the spec's `beforeAll`.

## Windows don't appear (decided 2026-10-09)

`npm run e2e` never shows its windows: they were opening centred, over whatever you were doing. A
hidden window still animates (`backgroundThrottling` is off in test mode) and Playwright still
composites it, so the pixel baselines and the review stills are unaffected — the whole suite passes
hidden.

- **To watch a run:** `STAR_CHART_TEST_SHOW=1 npm run e2e` (or any single spec). The window is pinned
  to the top-left of the primary display, and opens without taking focus.
- **`STAR_CHART_TEST_DPR=2`** launches with that devicePixelRatio (default 1), for checks that depend on it.
- **`npm run drive`** always shows its window: watching the app is the point of it.

## Taking ADO away (slice 5)

The fake ADO org can be switched off mid-run, from the main process, with no test-only surface in
production: `app.evaluate(() => globalThis.__starChartFakeTransport.offline = true)` (see
`tests/e2e/offline.spec.ts`). Three more affordances, all test-mode only:
- `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL` (a regex on the URL) with `STAR_CHART_FAKE_FAIL_STATUS` (500 by default; 401
  for a dead token, 403/404 for a refusal that keeps the last known facts).
- `STAR_CHART_PROJECTS_TTL_MS=1`: the project list is normally remembered for 30 s, which would hide an
  offline start; this asks every time, as a real launch does.
- The `reboot()` and `forgetScopes()` test hooks start the app's data over, as a launch does.

## Shared helpers (`tests/e2e/launch.ts`)

`launchApp`, `settle`, `clickNode`, `enterNodeByKey`, `keyOf`, the v0 walks (`openCometCrew`,
`openFeature101`) and `launchGallery` live here, and so does **`frames(page, n = 2)`** (23 F5): it
resolves once the page has drawn `n` more frames. Read what a seek or a setter drew after
`await frames(page)`, never after a fixed `waitForTimeout`, which under load can pass with no frame
drawn; don't write another copy in a spec. (In-page loops that sample every frame,
`await new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(r))` inside one `page.evaluate`, are samplers, not
waits, and stay where they are.)

**Waiting under load.** A machine running four specs draws fewer, longer frames, and the chart's
clock advances at most 100 ms a frame (`ChartApp.ts`). So bound a played stretch by the playhead
(`session().x`) or by the condition itself (the body arrived, enough moves judged), not by wall time:
`board`'s travel runs until the body arrives (bounded by 8 s of playhead), and `solar-dense`'s facing
check plays until 30 decisive moves are judged. To prove a de-flake, run the spec under load, e.g.
`npx playwright test --grep @keystone &` beside `npx playwright test <spec> --repeat-each=3` (build once
first, `npx electron-vite build`: the two runs share `out/`).

**Touch.** `touch.spec.ts` sends real touches through the DevTools protocol
(`page.context().newCDPSession(page)`, `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`): Playwright's `touchscreen` needs a
context made with `hasTouch`, which an Electron window can't be given. Chromium turns them into touch
events and pointer events with `pointerType: 'touch'`, as a touchscreen would.

## Isolation and parallel runs

Every launch gets its own `userData` (`tests/e2e/launch.ts`): never the developer's real cache. A spec
that relaunches on the same cache passes `STAR_CHART_DB_DIR`, and its `userData` sits beside that
folder. Specs run four at a time (`E2E_WORKERS` to change it). Tests inside a spec run in order; most
share one app and walk a story, so a test can depend on the ones before it. Keystone tests are chosen
to pass on their own after the spec's `beforeAll`.

# Star Chart: notes for the sluice's agents

The sluice's planner, reviewer, auditor and fixer read this file. The hard rules in CLAUDE.md
(fixture data only, never a real PAT, the app never writes to ADO, `src/shared/` pure, Pixi v8 only) apply
on top of it. Grow it from evidence: each lens below is here because a review caught it in v1.3, or
because it escaped.

## Sources of truth
- **Values:** every constant with a row in `docs/15-reference.md` changes with its row, in the same edit.
  `tests/unit/docTables.test.ts` fails until they match.
- **Normative docs:** `docs/02-domain-rules.md` §1 (invariants, INV-*) and `docs/03-contracts.md`
  (shapes, IPC, launch variables). A departure means amending the doc in the same change, and saying so
  in the run record.
- **Standing rules R1–R14:** `docs/13-game-design.md` §1, and the active scope doc's Rules. The ones
  reviews cite most: R3 (the outside matches the inside), R4 (counts first, no reflow), R9 (the drawn
  count is the true count), R11 (an object arrives before its label), R12 (ADO words first, the metaphor
  beside them).
- **Art that shows a work state:** `docs/09-signal-ladder.md`. **Layout and sizing:**
  `docs/08-layout-solver.md`, which records what hasn't worked.

## Review lenses
- **The effect where it's meant:** check the change on the busy fixtures it's for (Halcyon's Pulsar and
  Quasar pods), not only on the default scene. In v1.3, a new setting passed every test and did nothing
  on the busy pods.
- **Shared Pixi resources:** `destroy(true)` and texture or geometry teardown can free resources the main
  chart shares. Check that the chart still renders after the new view closes. This one froze the chart.
- **ADO failure semantics** (`docs/04-ado-ingestion.md` §6): a 401 on a scope-gated call (threads,
  builds, boards) means a missing scope, not a dead token. One 5xx on one item never fails a sync. Reads
  go through the throttle, and are deferred where the stream defers.
- **Users' caches:** a migration must not wipe what it doesn't need to. Prefer clearing checkpoints, so
  history re-reads lazily, over clearing facts or team lists. Check the first launch after an upgrade.
- **The drawn count is the true count (R9):** no `+N` beside a free slot, no object without a reason it
  can state, and counts that match what's drawn.
- **Frame budget:** dense scenes (Pulsar, 20 captains) sit near the p95 budget. Any per-object filter or
  extra pass needs a before-and-after perf run (`tests/e2e/perf.spec.ts`).
- **Electron surfaces:** drag and drop, navigation and file dialogs. A drop anywhere off the chart must
  never navigate the window. Test-only seams work only in unpackaged builds.
- **Mode and state that outlive a session:** anything that switches mode (fixture or ADO, a tour) must
  survive Cmd-Q without leaving the user stuck.

## How to verify here
- **Tests for the files you touched:** `tests/README.md` maps code areas to e2e specs. Run them with
  `npm run e2e:spec -- <names>`, plus `npm run e2e:keystone` (~40 s). Never run the full suite per item.
- **Seeing a change:** `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` (examples in `tests/drive/steps/`) takes stills of
  the real app. Put stills meant for the human gate in the item's work folder, and name them in the block
  note.
- **Art:** `npm run gallery` shows every object at every stage, including reduced motion.
- **Goldens:** update only the golden your item meant to move; check its diff line by line.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/scenarios/` (invented names only); the Halcyon demo's coverage is guarded by
  `halcyonCoverage.test.ts`.
- **Shared `out/`:** e2e, drive, build and gallery all rebuild it, so one at a time (`with-lock.sh` when
  parallel).

## Vocabulary
The metaphor is in `docs/12-glossary.md`: galaxy, star, planet, captain, station, pod. Use the ADO name
first in anything a user reads (R12).
tests/unit/maneuvers.test.ts
tests/unit/commands.test.ts
tests/unit/stationArrival.test.ts

# Pacing ledger

Where each pod's replay time goes at 1x, from the engine's own schedule and plan (read-only; `npm run pacing`). Seconds are to 0.1.
The time frame and the playing/held split are in schedule time and sum to the schedule length (Schedule s). Total s is the wall time at 1x once the director's adaptive speed is counted (27 E5b); they differ only on a pod whose beats are sped. The rule table charges each stretch of a beat to its lead maneuver (the one that ends last) and phase; `hold` is a crew's turn staying out after the last phase. Waiting is maneuver-seconds (maneuvers overlap, so it is not wall time), and its causes are inferred from the plan, not read from the engine's queue. Carry (P-10) is measured.

  with) and `short?` (27 E4d: the phases of a shorter play, keyed by the form it shortens, `plain` or a

  sorted). Unaccented beats plan `agent.light` only, gated by `Engagement`.

# Packet F2: Summon on the fly
Risk: medium (schedule: every pod with a summon; the engine's sequencer and the renderer's movers) · Start commit: 61e4958

Built in one conversation without subagents (the run's instruction): this file is the plan as built, and it
records the decisions the scope left open. No planner or reviewer agent ran, so there is no `plan-1.json` or
`review-1.*`; `build-1.json` is the build record.

## Acceptance (27 F2, unchanged)
- A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors.
- A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place, and the station's act
  starts within 50 ms of the blip.
- 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated, and the packet names each change.
- The ledger shows the saving per pod.

## Approach (as built)
1. **The rule** (`pace.ts`): `facility.enter`'s phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival: gather 715, act 1200
   (1915 ms; was tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600 = 2815). A new `PaceRule.pass?: true` marks it a **pass**.
2. **The sequencer** (`maneuvers.ts`), for a flying pass (`Draft.pass`):
   - `crewTimes(phases, pass)`: the ship leaves at the claim (the act's start, the blip). Its plate opens there,
     is whole for `NOTE_MIN_MS`, then folds (`closeMs = claim + CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS`). `passNoteMs` is when the
     plate has folded.
   - `durMs` is its phases alone (no held turn). `releaseOf` gives the claim. `heldMs` (attention and the beat's
     length) runs to `passNoteMs`, so the plate keeps its place while it is read.
   - `crewBusy` (P4): the captain's next flying sortie may set its gather off at the blip (`nearStartMs` with no
     work end). A non-flying next maneuver (the tender's `attachment.open`, which waits for the summon anyway)
     still starts at the summon's end.
   - `nearWaits` never parks a pass. `releaseOfPlay` and `passPlay(m)` read the pass from the rule id, as
     `flyingPlay` does.
3. **The renderer.**
   - `Pass` mover (`movers.ts`): two Hermite legs share the spot and the velocity there. The ship reaches the spot
     as the gather ends, then carries on to its layout place (its rest), easing in. When the way on doubles back,
     it is heading square to the way in, so it swings past the spot and never brakes at it. The second leg's time
     is the flight's, scaled by the distances, within `PASS_ON_MIN_S` and `PASS_ON_MAX_S` (0.45–1.2 s, 15 §10).
   - The pass keeps the node until its plate has folded (`crewOpen`), at home if it gets there first.
   - Hand-off: when a move takes over a pass in flight (`FxRunner.move`), it gets the pass's velocity
     (`takeCarried`). A `Sortie` or another `Pass` then sets off at that speed, so a summoner whose next sortie
     starts at the blip flies straight on.
   - A ship new to the scene (K-13) drops in at the spot.
   - `pursue` takes `pass` and `noteS`. The interpreter names the crew with `crewTimes(m.phases, passPlay(m))`,
     and `crew()` reads a `Pass`'s `crewOpen`.
4. **The choreography** (`stationJumpIn.ts`): gather is the pass (or a guest at the spot for `fly + noteS`). The
   act's first call is **the call blip**, `jumpRing` on the summoner's live anchor (`drawnR × 1.6`). In the same
   instant come the art's `jump`, the At-rest blue flare, and `jumpRing` on the station. One function draws both
   rings, so the hue, the expansion ratio (0.7 → 1.6), the duration and the alpha are the same by construction.
   The tell ring, the gather's fold ring and the land ring are gone. Under reduced motion `pursue` snaps (it isn't
   issued), so the ship stays at its place: the blip plays there, and so does the arrival.
5. **The ledger.**
   - `beforeF2(rules)` (`scripts/pacing-ledger.ts`) restores the old rule: the four phases, no `pass`. Every Built
     row before F2, C2's candidates and `sweep.test`'s Comet pin run on it, so none of their numbers move.
   - New Built rows on all seven pods (Meteor too, `all`): **F2**, undirected (the schedule's own saving), and
     **F2+**, with every lever (what the app plays).
6. **Docs.** 15 §7 (the maneuvers row, 1915 ms; the actions row), 15 §8 (the effect audit's jump-in rows), 15 §10
   (a new row, *A pass's way on*), 13 §6 (the jump-in row), 05 §8 (M-13, T-1, P-7), 03 (`PaceRule.pass`,
   `crewTimes(…, pass)`, `PursueArgs.pass/noteS`; **an amendment to a normative doc**, called out here and in the
   block note).

## Decisions taken here (no one to ask; recorded per the run's instruction)
- **"Its plate rides with the ship for NOTE_MIN_MS"** reads as the plate being *whole* for `NOTE_MIN_MS`, with the
  unfurl and fold on top: 22 B9's rule that the animations count toward no minimum. A first cut that counted the
  fold inside 1.8 s left the name whole for about 0.65 s. `solar-dense`'s turn spec caught it: too short to read.
- **"The rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival"**: gather and act only. The land's settle ring (a
  repeat the effect audit already muted) and the tell ring go. The gather's fold ring goes too, so the blip is the
  one call (the effect audit's rows are marked `cut`).
- **Blip size**: 1.6 × the summoner's drawn radius, in the station ring's shape. "The same ring shape" is the same
  ring at the caller's scale, not the station's size (a station-sized ring on the ship would cover the station).
- **The next place**: the ship carries on to its layout place unless a later move takes it over. The engine
  lets a flying next sortie set off at the blip, and the renderer hands the speed on. In today's beats the
  tender's `attachment.open` sits between two summons by one captain and keeps them busy, so in Meteor's opening
  the ship passes, heads home and is called out again. F3's summon chain replaces that run with one path.
- **The ledger's saving per pod** is two rows. Under the director's speed lever, a pod near the 300 s target uses
  the saving to pull fewer levers rather than to play shorter (F2+ Pulsar 0.0 s, Meteor −7.5 s; Pulsar keeps its
  72 light forms as moments). So the undirected F2 row is the schedule's own saving.

## Goldens and pinned numbers that moved (each named)
- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: every pod's `estimateMs` (shorter summons). Quasar and Pulsar get a new
  tempo. Pulsar's levers lose `light` (72 light forms back to moments): the saving gives the director room.
- `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-ledger.{md,json}`: every pod's tables, regenerated; the Built section gains the F2
  and F2+ rows. `pacing-built.json`: the 14 new rows, with no existing row changed. `pacing-candidates.json`:
  unchanged.
- No other golden moved (`sprint-pods.*`, `solar.*`, `meridian.*`, `halcyon-meteor.*` are projections or v0
  schedules that don't plan `facility.enter`'s phases).
- Tests changed with the rule: `commands.test` (the jump-in's calls; a new F2 test), `maneuvers.test` (two new F2
  tests; the acts-in-order property treats a pass as its captain's flight alone when only the crew ties two
  maneuvers), `sweep.test` (its Comet pin runs on `beforeF2`), `pacingBuilt.test` (new F2 rows; the frozen-rows
  filter leaves F rows out), `solar-dense.spec` (the turn spec reads a pass, *Opened it*, as riding: whole
  ≥ 1.7 s, not parked).

content.text:
F2 is built and committed as `982de53 sluice(F2): Summon on the fly` on `bench`. Nothing was pushed. All four acceptance lines pass. There was no independent review, because no subagents ran, so block F's audit will be the first outside look.

**What changed**
- **Engine:** the station jump-in (`facility.enter`) now has just a flight (715 ms) and an arrival (1200 ms), 1915 ms in all, down from 2815. The summoner is released at the moment it passes the spot, holds no turn there, and is never parked to wait for its next sortie.
- **Renderer:** a new mover flies the ship through the spot without slowing, then on to its rest. If its next sortie takes over at that moment, it starts at the ship's current speed.
- **The blip:** as the ship passes, it gives one call blip. The station's jump, flare and ring start at that same instant. One function draws both rings, so they share hue and shape. Under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly, and both play at its place.
- **Docs:** 15 §7, §8 and §10, 13 §6 and 05 §8 are updated. 03 (normative) is amended for the new rule flag and mover arguments; the item's build record notes this.

**Checks**
- Typecheck and lint are clean, and all 1723 unit tests pass.
- New unit tests cover the acceptance line: the summoner's flight has no hold, wait or return leg, and the station's act starts 0 ms after the blip.
- The jump-in gallery cell loops and clears in full and reduced motion with no console errors.
- e2e passes: gallery-assets, solar, solar-play and montage-names (52 tests), solar-dense (21) and keystone (43). Meteor's 1024×640 case is still the expected failure that F5 will fix.
- I didn't run the full `npm run e2e`.

**The ledger's saving per pod.** I measured the saving two ways:

| Pod | Saved, director off (s) | Saved, director on (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Comet | 0.9 | 0.9 |
| Nova | 2.9 | 2.9 |
| Quasar | 21.3 | 4.7 |
| Pulsar | 24.3 | 1.7 |
| Convoy Planning | 8.8 | 8.8 |
| Harbor | 5.1 | 5.1 |
| Meteor | 13.9 | −8.2 |

The director-off figure is the schedule's own saving. Pods near the 300 s target spend the saving on pulling fewer of the director's levers instead of playing shorter.
